head: 7e6241c
task: P16.10a T16 — Proto constant-resolution ownership audit (ANALYSIS ONLY)
question: Can one Proto be shared across two independent Vm instances? Is moving resolution to closure/load/VM-binding time clean?
verdict: NOT CLEAN — the mutable constants_resolved design needs architectural attention first. The Proto is NOT strictly VM-bound.

fields.k: []Constant — mutable constant pool. resolveProtoConstants mutates .str entries in-place, replacing compile-time LuaString pointers (seed-0 hash) with VM-interned pointers (VM-seed hash).
fields.constants_resolved: bool — mutable flag. Set true by resolveProtoConstants. Prevents re-resolution. After resolution, deinit skips freeing strings in k (they are VM-owned).
fields.resolved_values: []vm.Value — VM-allocated array. Allocated from self.alloc (VM allocator) in resolveProtoConstants. Contains VM-interned string pointers.
fields.p: []const *Proto — child protos. resolveProtoConstants does NOT recurse into p.

proto_structure.deinit_ownership: bytecode.zig:503-529: deinit checks constants_resolved to decide whether to free strings in k. If resolved, strings are VM-owned (not freed). resolved_values is freed if len > 0.

mutates: proto.k: replaces .str constants with VM-interned pointers (vm.zig:6696-6704)
resolveProtoConstants.recursion_note: Does NOT recurse into proto.p. Child protos are resolved lazily on their first pushBytecodeExecFrame call. This means a Proto tree may be partially resolved — some protos by VM1, others by VM2 if shared.

preResolveUndumpedConstants.called_from: undump path — after loading bytecode file
preResolveUndumpedConstants.recursion_note: DOES recurse into proto.p (vm.zig:23334-23336). This is the correct pattern for tree-wide resolution.
preResolveUndumpedConstants.key_difference: Does NOT mutate proto.k (strings were already interned during undump via undumpInternCallback). Only builds resolved_values from existing k.

locations: vm.zig:14174-14185: OP_TAILCALL handler — reads k for debug name resolution
vm.zig:22271-22278: gcMarkBytecodeProto — marks string constants in k for GC
vm.zig:24296-24430: funcnamefromcode equivalent — reads k[kidx].str.bytes() for debug names
vm.zig:23427: cloneStrippedProto — shares k with clone
vm.zig:23323: preResolveUndumpedConstants — reads k to build resolved_values
k_read_after_resolution.implication: After resolution, k contains VM-interned string pointers. All these read sites use VM-specific pointers. If the Proto is shared with another VM, these reads return pointers from the wrong VM string table.

cloneStrippedProto.borrowing_note: vm.zig:23441-23444: The cloned proto borrows resolved_values and k — it must NOT free them in deinit. Setting constants_resolved=true prevents deinit from freeing strings in k (also borrowed).
cloneStrippedProto.risk: If original is freed first, clone has dangling pointers to k strings and resolved_values. If clone is freed first, it skips freeing (correct), but original may double-free.

closure_proto_field.type: ?*const bc.Proto — raw pointer, no VM association
closure_proto_field.implication: A Closure holds a raw Proto pointer. Nothing prevents the same Proto from being referenced by Closures in different VMs.

dump_undump.dump: src/lua/dump.zig:231-290: Serializes k constants to binary format (string bytes). Does NOT share Proto pointers. Safe.
dump_undump.undump: src/lua/undump.zig:424-432: Creates fresh protos with constants_resolved=false. Safe — fresh protos, VM-bound at undump time.

vm_binding_mechanism.evidence: No vm_owner field on Proto. No VM association check in resolveProtoConstants. No mechanism prevents a Proto from being used by two different VMs.

cross_vm_scenario.description: VM1 loads a chunk, resolves Proto (mutates k, allocates resolved_values from VM1 allocator). Proto pointer is shared with VM2 (via cloneStrippedProto or direct pointer sharing).
vm1_resolution: proto.k .str entries replaced with VM1-interned pointers
vm2_usage: VM2 uses VM1-interned string pointers in k and resolved_values
VM2 GC does not track VM1 strings → GC may collect them
vm1_destruction: VM1 string table freed → k .str entries become dangling pointers
VM1 allocator freed → resolved_values becomes dangling pointer
VM2 crashes on next access to k or resolved_values

architectural_issues.evidence: vm.zig:6696-6704: resolveProtoConstants replaces .str in k with VM-interned pointers. After mutation, k contains VM-specific pointers that cannot be used by another VM.
architectural_issues.fix_direction: Stop mutating k. Build resolved_values directly from compile-time strings without modifying k. Free compile-time strings separately (or not at all if arena-allocated).

architectural_issues.evidence: vm.zig:6710: resolved_values allocated from self.alloc (VM allocator). If Proto is shared, cross-VM allocation ownership issue.
architectural_issues.fix_direction: Make resolved_values Proto-owned (with Proto-owned allocator or reference counting). Or allocate from a Proto-owned arena.

architectural_issues.issue: cloneStrippedProto shares resolved state via fragile borrowing
architectural_issues.evidence: vm.zig:23441-23446: Clone shares resolved_values and constants_resolved with original. No reference counting. Dangling pointers if original freed first.
architectural_issues.fix_direction: Either give the clone its own resolved_values, or reference-count the shared array.

architectural_issues.evidence: No vm_owner field on Proto. No check in resolveProtoConstants. Closure.proto is a raw ?*const bc.Proto pointer.
architectural_issues.fix_direction: Add vm_owner: ?*Vm field on Proto. Check in resolveProtoConstants: if vm_owner != null and vm_owner != self, either re-resolve or error.

architectural_issues.evidence: vm.zig:6694-6722: No loop over proto.p. Child protos resolved lazily. A shared Proto tree may have protos resolved by different VMs.
architectural_issues.fix_direction: Make resolveProtoConstants recurse into proto.p (like preResolveUndumpedConstants does at vm.zig:23334-23336).

conclusion.verdict: Moving resolution to closure/load/VM-binding time is NOT clean with the current design. The mutable constants_resolved design needs architectural attention first.
required_changes_before_moving_resolutio: 1. Stop mutating k (build resolved_values directly from compile-time strings)
3. Add VM-binding mechanism (vm_owner field + check in resolveProtoConstants)
4. Make resolveProtoConstants recurse into child protos
5. Rethink cloneStrippedProto sharing (reference counting or independent resolution)
conclusion.puc_comparison: PUC Lua stores constants in runtime TValue format directly in Proto.k (lobject.h:614). The compiler interns strings through the same global string table as the runtime, so constant pool strings are already interned and VM-neutral (there is only one global state per lua_State). Our design defers resolution to first execution and mutates k in-place, creating VM-specific state that prevents Proto sharing.
